title: 第8章　变化中的迁入者，转型中的伊斯坦布尔：《我脑袋里的怪东西》——一个男人与他的城市的爱情故事
originalTitle: CHAPTER 8 Changing Migrants, Transforming Istanbul: A Strangeness in My Mind as a Love Story of a Man and His City

zh: 第8章　变化中的迁入者，转型中的伊斯坦布尔：《我脑袋里的怪东西》——一个男人与他的城市的爱情故事
en: CHAPTER 8 Changing Migrants, Transforming Istanbul:
as a Love Story of a Man and His City

zh: 奥尔罕·帕慕克的第九部小说《Kafamda Bir Tuhaflık》（《我脑袋里的怪东西》）于2014年末出版，讲述了独特的街头小贩麦夫鲁特，从少年时迁往伊斯坦布尔，到年过五十的故事，时间跨度从20世纪70年代初一直到21世纪头十年末。帕慕克通过描写麦夫鲁特的内心世界，逐渐揭示标题中暗示的“怪”；这个内心世界的中心，是他对自己所生活的城市——伊斯坦布尔——的依恋。
en: Orhan Pamuk’s ninth novel

), published at the end of 2014, tells the story of the idiosyncratic street vendor Mevlut from his migration to Istanbul as teenager until he is a man in his fifties, covering a timespan from the early 1970s to the late 2000s. Pamuk reveals Mevlut’s strangeness slowly, which he implies in the title, by depicting his inner world at the centre of which lies his attachment to Istanbul, the city he lives in.

zh: 在《我脑袋里的怪东西》中，帕慕克从多个方面处理城市权利概念。借用阿塞夫·巴亚特的术语，当“普通人的静默蚕食”（Bayat 2013，80）成为迁入者的生存策略时，城市权利便处于小说的中心。然而，由于主人公具有丰富的内心层次，借助列斐伏尔关于城市作为
的观念，这在书中又演变为不普通者的静默蚕食。在小说场景中，被称为衰败、正处在城市改造前夕的塔尔拉巴舍街区，占据突出位置。某些与城市权利相关的主题，例如居住在市中心的权利，便通过这一地方得到讨论。帕慕克采用独特的叙事情境，让人物同叙述者共同承担叙述任务，邀请读者通过迁入者的眼睛看待小说的问题，而非追随一位城市叙述者的权威。
en: In

, Pamuk addresses the concept of the right to the city in various ways. In “the quiet encroachment of the ordinary” (Bayat 2013, 80), to borrow Asef Bayat’s term, as a survival strategy of migrants, the right to the city is at the centre of the novel. Yet, this evolves into the quiet encroachment of the unordinary in the book, through the Lefebvrian notion of the city as

, owing to its sophisticated protagonist. In the setting of the novel, Tarlabaşı, a so-called deteriorated neighbourhood on the verge of urban transformation, is in a prominent position. Certain themes related to the right to the city, such as the right to live in the city centre, are treated with reference to this place. With his unique approach to the narrative situation, where characters share the task of narration with the narrator, Pamuk invites his readers to look at the novel’s issues through the eyes of migrants rather than follow the authority of an urban narrator.

zh: 第一章的结尾，尤其是叙述声音的语调，为小说的核心主题提供了线索：
en: The ending of the first chapter, particularly with the tone of the narrative voice, gives clues about the central themes of the novel:

zh: 拉伊哈以前曾来过伊斯坦布尔一次，参加姐姐的婚礼。但她还是谦卑地问：“现在这里就是伊斯坦布尔了吗？”
en: Rayiha had already been to Istanbul once for her elder sister’s wedding. But still she humbly asked, “Is this Istanbul now?”

zh: “我想，卡尔塔尔也算伊斯坦布尔吧，”麦夫鲁特带着熟悉此地的自信说。“不过还得走一段。”他指着前方的王子群岛，发誓有一天要带她去。
en: “Kartal counts as Istanbul, I suppose,” said Mevlut, with the confidence of familiarity. “But there’s still a way to go.” He pointed out the Princes’ Islands ahead of them and vowed to take her there one day.

zh: 在拉伊哈短暂的一生中，他们一次也没有去过。（Pamuk 2015，13—14）
en: Not once during Rayiha’s brief life would they ever do this. (Pamuk 2015, 13–14)

zh: “谦卑地”和“熟悉此地的自信”等措辞，暗示在伊斯坦布尔生活过所带来的声望。这里强调拉伊哈的谦卑，给了麦夫鲁特展示城市知识的机会，也预示两人关系将如何发展：善良而支持他的拉伊哈，会让麦夫鲁特感到被爱、被支持。此时的场景是城市郊外的卡尔塔尔。隔海相望的王子群岛，是伊斯坦布尔风景最美的地区之一。这幅图景仿佛一个意象，暗示伊斯坦布尔的不同面孔。生活在伊斯坦布尔，可能意味着每天从卡尔塔尔这样偏远的区域通勤数小时去市中心，却也可能意味着游览群岛的乐趣。这座城市将这一切都容纳其中，因为生活在伊斯坦布尔，既可能意味着无尽的挑战，也可能意味着独特的快乐。引文的最后一句，暗示拉伊哈的早逝。这句话或许也隐含着对反迁入者话语的反驳：那种话语认为，迁入者因无知而不去观光，也不参观伊斯坦布尔的历史场所。这里，叙述声音中的同情语调，暗示经济及其他因素使麦夫鲁特和拉伊哈始终未能游览群岛。这一语调表明了全书对伊斯坦布尔新居民的立场。
en: Words such as “humbly” and “confidence of familiarity” imply the prestige of having spent time in Istanbul. The emphasis on Rayiha’s humbleness here, which indulges Mevlut with the opportunity to demonstrate his knowledge about the city, is a foreshadowing of the way their relationship will evolve: Rayiha as a good-natured and supportive person will make Mevlut feel loved and supported. The setting at this point is Kartal on the outskirts of the city. The Princes’ Islands, one of the most picturesque areas of Istanbul, appears just across the sea. This picture functions like an imagery hinting at the different faces of Istanbul. Living in Istanbul might mean commuting for hours every day from a remote area like Kartal to the centre of the city, yet it might mean the pleasure of visiting the Islands. The city contains them all, as living in Istanbul can mean endless challenges as well as unique pleasures. The last sentence in the excerpt is an indication of Rayiha’s early death. The sentence might also hint at a counter-argument to the anti-migrant discourse which suggests that migrants, because of ignorance, do not go sightseeing or visit historical places in Istanbul. Here, the sympathetic tone in the narrative voice implies the economic and other factors preventing Mevlut and Rayiha from ever visiting the Islands. This tone is a sign of the book’s stance regarding the new inhabitants of Istanbul.

zh: 如第3章所讨论的，阿塞夫·巴亚特把搭建棚屋、沿街叫卖等生存策略，描述为“蚕食”（2012，120），也称为“普通人的静默蚕食”（2013，80）。巴亚特强调，“通过这种蚕食，被剥夺者不断地在城市空间之中、围绕城市空间展开斗争”（2012，120）。沿街叫卖作为静默蚕食的一种形式，是《我脑袋里的怪东西》的核心母题。与街头贩卖工作相关的经验和情感，处于主人公麦夫鲁特精神世界的中心。他是乡村迁入者，是试图在伊斯坦布尔生存的穷人，却也是被塑造成内心丰富的个体的独特虚构人物。奥尔罕·帕慕克在一次访谈中认为，作家并不写
的穷人的小说（2014c）。梅廷·杰拉尔回应这一说法，指出来自包括土耳其在内的世界各地的多位作家，尤其那些遵循社会主义现实主义传统的作家，已经成功描绘过贫穷人物的个体性（2015，10）。很难不同意杰拉尔。不过，帕慕克其实并未声称，自己是文学史上第一个写出以穷人为个体的小说的人。他更像是在说明自己小说主人公的独特之处，下面将对此展开讨论。
en: As discussed in Chapter 3, survival strategies such as building shanty houses or vending on the streets are described by Asef Bayat as “encroachment” (2012, 120), as well as “quiet encroachment of the ordinary” (2013, 80). Bayat stresses that “through this encroachment, the dispossessed are constantly engaged in struggles in and about the urban space” (2012, 120). Vending on streets, a form of quiet encroachment, is a central motif in

. Experiences and emotions related with working as a street vendor are central to the psyche of Mevlut, the protagonist. He is a rural migrant, a poor man trying to survive in Istanbul, yet a unique fictional character portrayed as a sophisticated individual. In an interview, Orhan Pamuk argues that authors do not write the novel of the poor person

(2014c). Metin Celal, responding to this claim, asserts that various authors from different parts of the world including Turkey, particularly those who follow a socialist realist tradition, have successfully depicted the individuality of their poor characters (2015, 10). It is impossible to disagree with Celal. However, Pamuk does not really claim to be the first person in literary history to have written the novel of the poor person as an individual. He is rather trying to make a point about the idiosyncrasy of his novel’s protagonist which is discussed below.

zh: 临近全书结尾的第七部开头，有一句让-雅克·卢梭的题辞：“只有走路时，我才能思考”（561）。麦夫鲁特一生都觉得，在户外工作比待在室内更好受。他做街头小贩，白天卖酸奶或米饭，晚上额外出去卖钵扎。
夜间卖钵扎，并不只是麦夫鲁特挣钱的方式，其中快乐的成分占据主导。事实上，卖钵扎并不是很赚钱的行当。当他紧张、不快或忧郁时，卖钵扎能抚慰他的心灵，因为这样一来，他便会在城市街道上走好几个小时。在这些漫长的夜晚，他觉得城市在对他说话。无论白天工作，还是夜间卖钵扎，他都享受待在外面的自由。从这个意义上说，麦夫鲁特像一个
en: Towards the end of the book, at the beginning of the seventh part, there is an epigraph from J. J. Rousseau: “I can only meditate when I’m walking” (561). Throughout his life, Mevlut feels better when he is working outside rather than indoors. He works as a street vendor, selling yoghurt or rice in the daytime, and goes out to sell boza at night as an extra job.

Selling boza at night is not something Mevlut simply does to earn money, as the pleasure aspect is predominant. In fact, selling boza is not such a profitable occupation. When he is stressed, unhappy or melancholic, selling boza soothes Mevlut’s soul, since to do that he walks in the streets of the city for hours. During these long nights, he feels that the city is speaking to him. Either in his daytime jobs, or at night selling boza, he enjoys the freedom of being outside. Mevlut resembles a
in this sense.

zh: 正如穆拉特·贝尔盖指出的，从文化和收入而言，无法把麦夫鲁特描述为
（2014，21）。然而，无论他在社会与文化上离
多远，在心理上却很接近。基思·泰斯特描写波德莱尔的诗人的话——后者也许是文化与文学史上最典型的
——竟也适用于麦夫鲁特，这一点令人惊讶：“一个因寻求意义而被从私人领域驱向公共领域的人。只有身体不在家时，他在存在意义上才感到如在家中”（2006，2）。
为了乐趣而漫步城中，麦夫鲁特却是作为小贩走上街头。这是外在现实。至于内在现实，麦夫鲁特拥有波德莱尔式诗人的灵魂。泰斯特强调，“波德莱尔式的诗人”有“为自己创造大都市空间与公共景象的意义和重要性的能力”（4）。小贩麦夫鲁特也是如此。他在行走时，以丰富深刻的眼光感知周围世界，许多受过教育的城市人也未必做得到。麦夫鲁特与
之间的相似，不大可能只是巧合。正如贝尔盖承认的，很难设想，像帕慕克这样广泛了解世界文学的作家，会不知道麦夫鲁特与
之间的相似（私人通信，2015年11月26日）。帕慕克让麦夫鲁特这个贫穷迁入者具有
——一个多少带有精英色彩的人物——的眼光，从而模糊了城市精英与乡村迁入者之间的界线。
en: As Murat Belge points out, in terms of culture and income it would not be possible to describe Mevlut as a
(2014, 21). However, no matter how far he is from a
socially and culturally, he is close to one psychologically. It is striking to see how Keith Tester’s words describing Baudelaire’s poet, probably the most characteristic

in cultural and literary history, are also valid for Mevlut: “a man who is driven out of the private and into the public by his own search for meaning. He is the man who is only at home existentially when he is not at home physically” (2006, 2). Unlike the

who strolls through the city for pleasure, Mevlut is out on the streets as a vendor. This is the outer reality. Where the inner reality is concerned, Mevlut carries the soul of the Baudelairean poet. Tester emphasises that “the Baudelairean poet” has “an ability to make for himself the meaning and the significance of the metropolitan spaces and the spectacle of the public” (4). This is also the case for Mevlut, the vendor. On his walks, Mevlut perceives the world around him with a sophisticated outlook, in a manner many educated urbanites would not be able to do. It is unlikely that parallels between Mevlut and the

are simple coincidence. As Belge acknowledges, it is difficult to assume that an author like Pamuk, who has a vast knowledge of world literature, would not be aware of the resemblance between Mevlut and the
(pers. comm., 26 November 2015). Embodying Mevlut, the poor migrant with the outlook of the
, a somewhat elite figure, Pamuk blurs the distinction between the elite urbanite and the rural migrant.

zh: 麦夫鲁特无尽的行走
en: Mevlut’s Endless Walks

zh: 帕慕克通过麦夫鲁特在城市行走的母题，突出他对伊斯坦布尔的热爱。夜间卖钵扎，对麦夫鲁特而言是一种生活方式：“每夜的漫长步行已不再只是工作的一部分；他觉得自己

这样做”（350）；而在宾博姆咖啡馆工作时，他感到一种幽闭感：“简直就像被锁链拴在店里”（362）。叙述者这样传达麦夫鲁特夜间卖钵扎的感受：“现在他感觉到，那些他在夜间卖钵扎的街道，与他脑中的宇宙，是同一个东西”（363）。心理叙述继续讲述街道对他的意义：“当然，对街道孤独的唯一解药，就是街道本身”（373）。叙述者补充，在宾博姆干了五年，使麦夫鲁特变成一个忧郁的人。有一次，他告诉朋友费尔哈特，自己总想一直卖钵扎（382）。
en: Pamuk accentuates Mevlut’s passion for Istanbul through the motif of his walks in the city. Selling boza at night is a way of life for Mevlut: “his long nightly walks weren’t just part of his job anymore; they were something he felt he

to do” (350); and when he is working at the Binbom cafe, he feels a sort of claustrophobia: “he may as well have been chained to the shop” (362). The narrator conveys Mevlut’s feelings about selling boza at night as follows: “he sensed, now, that the streets on which he sold boza in the night and the universe in his mind were one and the same” (363). The psycho-narration continues with the meaning of the streets for him: “of course the only antidote to the loneliness of the streets was the streets themselves” (373). The narrator adds that working at Binbom for five years has made Mevlut a melancholic person. At one point, he tells his friend Ferhat that he would always want to continue selling boza (382).

zh: 城市的历史遗产滋养了麦夫鲁特丰富的幻想世界。叙述者带着共情解释，历史痕迹如何提醒他，“我们的世界中还存在另一个领域”（391）。小说里的其他迁入者为在城市中取得的物质成就感到自豪时，麦夫鲁特却全神贯注于同伊斯坦布尔的灵魂建立联系。所有历史遗存——那些反映城市丰富历史遗产的神秘遗物，例如“一堵生着苔藓的老墙”（271），或一块“一直追溯到奥斯曼时代”的墓碑（273）——都吸引着他。这一切让这个“非伊斯坦布尔人”麦夫鲁特兴奋；而许多伊斯坦布尔人甚至不会留意这些细节，或者因为太习惯了，便将其当作城市肌理中寻常普通的要素而忽略。帕慕克在很大程度上通过麦夫鲁特同城市的关系来塑造他。回到上面的争论，萨伊特·法伊克或奥尔罕·凯末尔这样的作家，当然塑造过像麦夫鲁特一样、具有城市身份和个体性的穷人角色。帕慕克前述言论，也许只是想说明自己塑造麦夫鲁特这一工程的规模：极为深入地刻画这个穷人的独特之处，把他塑造成一个深爱城市生活的独特个体。
en: The historical heritage of the city nourishes Mevlut’s rich fantasy world. The narrator explains with empathy how traces of history remind him of the existence of “another realm within our world” (391). While other migrants in the novel are proud of their material achievements in the city, Mevlut is engrossed in connecting with the soul of Istanbul. All the remnants of history—enigmatic artefacts reflecting the rich historical heritage of the city, such as “a mossy old wall” (271) or a gravestone “dating all the way back to Ottoman times” (273)—appeal to him. All of these excite Mevlut the ‘non-Istanbulite’, details which many Istanbulites would not even notice, or simply ignore as usual and ordinary elements of the city fabric, maybe because they are too accustomed to them. To a large extent, Pamuk develops Mevlut through his relationship with the city. If we go back to the argument above, certainly authors such as Sait Faik or Orhan Kemal created characters from the poor who were individuals with an urban identity like Mevlut. With his words quoted above, Pamuk might simply be referring to the scale of his project of creating Mevlut, the poor man, with his idiosyncrasies in great depth, as a unique individual in love with urban life.

zh: 有了麦夫鲁特这样的人物，我们便可以从新的维度看待巴亚特关于“普通人的静默蚕食”的概念化（2013，80）。帕慕克描写贫穷迁入者在城市中的静默蚕食：在他的棚屋里，在他推着摊车的街道上。然而，就麦夫鲁特而言，静默蚕食不仅使迁入者得以在城市中生存，也使他能够对城市形成依恋。迁入者麦夫鲁特并非只是为了谋生而选择住在城市的人。他与城市的联系建立在热爱之上。他爱城市的历史遗产，爱它作为
的存在。帕慕克在书中不断强调麦夫鲁特内心世界的这一维度。因此，帕慕克并不只是从物质需要来讨论城市权利。麦夫鲁特的城市权利，还涉及与城市的社会文化联系，这可以通过城市作为
来解释。他爱作为
的城市。他既没有相应收入，也没有相应社交圈，无法成为城市高雅文化和艺术世界的一部分，也无法像游客那样观光。他从不这样漫步城市。然而，当他在市中心推着摊车，或提着钵扎篮子时，却在欣赏老建筑、墓地、人群，简言之，在欣赏城市的灵魂。他创造了完全属于自己的生活方式，借此将城市作为
来体验。
en: With a character like Mevlut, we can look at Bayat’s conceptualisation of “quiet encroachment of the ordinary” (2013, 80) through a new dimension. Pamuk addresses the quiet encroachment of the poor migrant in the city, in his shanty, on the streets with his stall. However, in Mevlut’s case, the quiet encroachment not only makes it possible for the migrant to survive in the city, but also enables him to develop an attachment to the city. Mevlut the migrant is not simply a person who chooses to live in the city to earn a living there. His ties with the city are based on passion. He is in love with the historical heritage of the city, with its

. Pamuk constantly emphasises this dimension of Mevlut’s inner world in the book. Consequently, Pamuk does not address the right to the city simply in terms of material needs. The right to the city in Mevlut’s case involves a social and cultural connection with the city which can be explained in terms of the city as
. He loves the city as

. He possesses neither the income nor the social circles to be a part of the high culture and art world of the city, or to go sightseeing like a tourist. He never does this kind of strolling through the city. However, as he pushes his stall or carries his boza basket in the centre of the city he enjoys old buildings, graveyards, crowds, simply the soul of the city. He invents his very own lifestyle which enables him to experience the city as

zh: 有些人把城市贫民仅仅看作被动者，巴亚特则提醒人们注意，他们具有寻找其他生存方式的潜力。帕慕克在小说中强调这一点，并将之推进到另一个维度：个体性。为谋生而挣扎的迁入者，可以通过城市经验发展出城市身份，成为个体。就麦夫鲁特而言，普通人的静默蚕食，似乎采取了不普通者的静默蚕食这一形式。
en: Bayat draws attention to the urban poor’s potential to find alternative ways to survive, as opposed to those who regard them as simply passive. In his novel Pamuk underlines this point, and takes it to a further dimension: that of individuality. The migrants struggling to earn their living can develop an urban identity and become individuals though their experiences in the city. In Mevlut’s case, the quiet encroachment of the ordinary seems to take the form of the quiet encroachment of the unordinary.

zh: 城市中的家
en: A Home in the City

zh: 如同大多数处理乡城迁移现象的作品，棚屋在《我脑袋里的怪东西》中，既作为场景，也作为主题，具有强烈的存在感。棚屋场景还承担核心功能：表现麦夫鲁特初到伊斯坦布尔时的孤独与隔绝感。小说第三部涵盖1968至1982年，从麦夫鲁特来到城市，直到他同拉伊哈结婚。这一部第二章题为“家：城市尽头的山丘”（46）。开篇第一句是：“家是一间
，一间棚屋”（46）。叙述者解释，麦夫鲁特的父亲大多时候把家称为“

”（棚屋），很少称之为家。棚屋只有一个房间，地面是泥土，外面有个简陋厕所（47）。家具只有这些：“一张旧桌、四把椅子、两张床（一张有弹簧，一张没有）、两个橱柜、两扇窗户和一个炉子”（47）。棚屋的气氛阴郁。在最初这些描写中，棚户住房与身处边缘彼此交织：“他们的房子位于城市边缘，在一座秃秃的、泥泞的山丘较低处，山上零星长着桑树，偶尔还有一棵无花果树”（49）。麦夫鲁特的父亲带他登上这一带最高的地方，指点四周：
en: As in most works which address the rural–urban migration phenomenon, the shanty, both as a setting and as a theme, has a strong presence in

. The shanty setting also has a central function in the representations of Mevlut’s feelings of solitude and isolation during the first phase of his time in Istanbul. The third part of the novel covers the period between 1968 and 1982, from Mevlut’s arrival in the city until his marriage with Rayiha. The second chapter of this part is entitled “Home: The Hills at the End of the City” (46). The chapter opens with the following sentence: “Home was a
, a slum house” (46). The narrator explains that Mevlut’s father most of the time refers to home as “

” (shanty) and rarely as home. The shanty has one room with a dirt floor, and a primitive toilet outside (47). There are only the following pieces of furniture: “an old table, four chairs, two beds (one with bedsprings and one without), two cupboards, two windows and a stove” (47). The atmosphere of the shanty is grim. Shanty housing and being on the periphery are intertwined in these initial descriptions: “their house was at the edge of the city, on the lower part of a balding, muddy hill dotted with mulberry trees, and with a fig tree here and there” (49). Mevlut’s father takes him to the highest point in the area to show him around:

zh: 从这里，可以看到迅速占据周围山丘的棚户区［……］、全城最大的墓地（津吉尔利库尤）、形形色色的工厂、汽车修理厂、作坊、仓库、药品和灯泡制造厂，以及远处城市幽灵般的轮廓，那里耸立着高楼与宣礼塔。城市本身及其街区——麦夫鲁特和父亲早晨卖酸奶、晚上卖钵扎，以及麦夫鲁特上学的地方——只是地平线上几块神秘的模糊影迹。（50）
en: From here, you could see the slums that were rapidly taking over the surrounding hills [...], the city’s biggest cemetery (Zincirlikuyu), factories of all shapes and sizes, garages, workshops, depots, medicine and lightbulb manufacturers, and, in the distance, the ghostly silhouette of the city with its tall buildings and its minarets. The city itself and its neighborhoods – where Mevlut and his father sold yogurt in the mornings and boza in the evenings, and where Mevlut went to school – were only mysterious smudges on the horizon. (50)

zh: 在边缘这样的氛围中生活，麦夫鲁特却并不是一个不快乐的人，并不觉得自己住在城市尽头山丘上的棚屋里，就是过着悲惨的生活。他更像是一个自足的人，凭借丰富的想象力，总能找到使心灵愉悦的东西。
en: Living in such an atmosphere on the periphery, Mevlut is not an unhappy person feeling that he is living in misery, in a shanty on a hill at the edge of the city. He is rather a self-sufficient person, always capable of finding entertainment for his mind owing to his rich imagination.

zh: 叙述者详细解释了建造棚屋的非正规程序（57—59）。相关段落强调，为了栖身而建棚屋，与为了出租而建棚屋，二者有所区别。棚户生活在不断拆除威胁下的脆弱性，也在这里出现。叙述者将棚屋描述为“四面墙和一个屋顶”（281）。帕慕克完成了一项艰难任务：不褒扬，也不谴责，而是现实地描绘棚屋的演变。面对棚户现象，他的立场是同情那些为栖身而建棚屋的人。不熟悉棚户住房的读者，通过现实主义描写，得以一窥这种生活。拉伊哈的妹妹萨米哈对自己与丈夫费尔哈特所住棚屋的评论（278），也被纳入，进一步展开这一主题。临近小说结尾，麦夫鲁特目睹自己初到城市时与父亲居住的棚屋被拆；呈现其感受的叙述声音充满共情：“轮到他自己那间单屋时，麦夫鲁特觉得心都碎了。他看着整个童年、吃过的饭、做过的作业、各种东西的气味、父亲睡梦中的咕哝声，成千上万的记忆，都在推土机铲斗的一次挥动中化为碎片”（559）。
en: The narrator explains the informal procedures for building a shanty in detail (57–59). In the related passage he stresses the difference between those who build shanties for shelter and those who build them for rent. The fragility of shanty dwelling life with the constant threat of demolition is also present here. The narrator describes the shanty as “four walls and a ceiling” (281). Pamuk accomplishes the difficult mission of painting a realistic picture of the evolution of shanties without praise or condemnation. His standpoint on the shanty phenomenon is one of empathy for those who build them for shelter. Readers who are unfamiliar with shanty housing get a glimpse of this life through its realistic depictions. The comments of Samiha, Rayiha’s sister, on the shanty where she lives with her husband Ferhat (278) are also included for elaboration of the theme. Towards the end of the novel, the narrative voice rendering Mevlut’s feelings as he watches the demolition of their shanty, where he lived with his father in his first years in the city, is full of empathy: “When the time came for his own one-room house, Mevlut felt his heart breaking. He observed his whole childhood, the food he’d eaten, the homework he’d done, the way things had smelled, the sound of his father grunting in his sleep, hundreds of thousands of memories all smashed to pieces in a single swipe of the bulldozer shovel” (559).

zh: 在迁移的较早几十年，大多数迁入者住棚屋，也有一些家庭住在市中心贫困街区的破旧公寓里；这些街区被贬称为衰败街区。还有一部分人，住在自己做门房的公寓楼的地下室住房中。棚屋与贫困街区在书中占有显著位置，地下室住房的生活却只被提及一次：萨米哈谈起朋友泽丽哈的家，说那是“门房的住处，比我们住的房间还小，甚至没有一扇窗”（285）。倘若是叙述者这样描写，听来可能像居高临下的同情；但这评论出自内部人，因此效果自然又温暖。
en: In the earlier decades of migration, the majority of migrants lived in shanties, while some migrant families lived in run-down apartments of poor neighbourhoods in the city centre which are pejoratively called deteriorated neighbourhoods. Another group of them lived in the basement flats of the apartment buildings where they worked as caretakers. While shanties and poor neighbourhoods have a strong presence in the book, the life in these basement flats is mentioned only once, when Samiha is talking about her friend Zeliha’s home as “the doorman’s quarters, which were smaller than the room we lived in lacking even a window” (285). If it was the narrator describing the place in this way, it could sound like sympathy from above, but as the comment comes from an insider, the effect is effortless and warm.

zh: 小说中有一处，将住在市中心破旧公寓，与住在边缘棚屋作比较。麦夫鲁特等候堂亲来访，因为房间里有气味，想打开窗户。拉伊哈担心女儿们着凉，问他：“难道他们在桑树山的房子，不也是这个味道？”（263）。麦夫鲁特回答：“不是。他们有那么大的花园，有电有自来水，什么都运转得顺顺当当。可我们在这里快乐得多”（263）。这些话反映了麦夫鲁特对叔叔的怨恨，因为过去在棚屋纠纷中，叔叔表现得自私。不过，其中也含有对住在市中心的满足：塔尔拉巴舍公寓中艰难的条件，似乎是生活在城市心脏地带的代价。作为小贩，麦夫鲁特总在公共空间里活动。据巴亚特说，“新自由主义城市是一座‘内外翻转的城市’”，“其中大量城市居民——底层民众——被迫在公共空间中经营、维生，或只是生活，也就是在街头、在规模庞大的‘户外经济’中活动”（2012，113）。倘若不住在塔尔拉巴舍这样的中心街区，麦夫鲁特就无法在夜间到城市的老街区卖钵扎。
en: In the novel, there is one instance of comparison between living in run-down apartments in the city centre and living in a shanty on the periphery. At one point, Mevlut, expecting his cousin’s visit, wants to open the windows because of the smell in the room. Rayiha, concerned that their daughters will feel cold, asks him: “doesn’t their house in Duttepe smell exactly like this?” (263). Mevlut responds her: “It doesn’t. They’ve got that huge garden, they’ve got electricity and running water, it’s all like clockwork. But we’re much happier here” (263). These words reflect Mevlut’s resentment towards his uncle for his selfishness in the past during the conflict over the shanty. However, it also has a connotation of satisfaction about living in the city centre: the challenging conditions of apartments in Tarlabaşı seem to be the cost of living at the heart of the city. As a vendor Mevlut is always out in public spaces. “The neoliberal city is a ‘city-inside-out,’” according to Bayat, “where a massive number of urban residents, the subaltern, become compelled to operate, subsist, or simply live on the public spaces – in the streets, in a substantial ‘out-doors economy’” (2012, 113). If Mevlut did not live in a central neighbourhood like Tarlabaşı he would not be able to sell boza at night in the old neighbourhoods of the city.

zh: 被污名化的街区：虚构与实情之间
en: Stigmatised Neighbourhoods: Between Fiction and Factuality

zh: 伊斯坦布尔两个遭受污名化最严重的街区，在小说场景中占据突出位置：塔尔拉巴舍与加齐。在小说前面的部分，虚构的棚户区灰山与桑树山是主要场景；麦夫鲁特搬离父亲的棚屋后，情况便发生变化。他在市中心所谓衰败街区塔尔拉巴舍租下公寓，这里便成为他的生活中心，因而也成为小说的中心。对这一地方的再现，在作品中不止一个语境里发挥作用：作为被污名化街区的塔尔拉巴舍，以及塔尔拉巴舍的城市改造。
en: Two of the most stigmatised neighbourhoods in Istanbul are in a prominent position in the setting of the novel: Tarlabaşı and Gazi. While in the earlier parts of the book, the fictional shanty towns of Kültepe and Duttepe are central to the setting, this changes with Mevlut’s moving out of his father’s shanty. As he rents an apartment in Tarlabaşı, a so-called deteriorated neighbourhood in the city centre, this area becomes the locus of his life, therefore of the novel. The representation of this place has a function in more than one context in the work: Tarlabaşı as a stigmatised neighbourhood, and the urban transformation in Tarlabaşı.

zh: 塔尔拉巴舍位于佩拉大街附近，直到20世纪30年代穆斯林家庭开始迁入之前，几乎只有少数族群在此居住、经商。
20世纪40年代，迁入这一地区的穆斯林增多；但此时，佩拉与塔尔拉巴舍仍以少数族群和黎凡特人为主。然而，财富税（1942—1943年）的实施，使大量企业与房产从他们手中转移到穆斯林人口手中。

1955年9月6—7日暴乱后，城市的许多非穆斯林居民，尤其是希腊人，出售部分房产后离开土耳其（Üsdiken 1995，218）。1964年法令生效后，35,000至40,000名希腊人被逐出土耳其（Demir and Akar 1999，157—158）。由于必须在极短时间内离境，他们无法出售房产，这些房产后来被无权处置的人出租给第三方。这些变化对塔尔拉巴舍产生了直接而巨大的影响：“尤其在20世纪60年代之后，由于国内迁移与产权结构变化，塔尔拉巴舍及周边成为低收入群体居住的地区。来自安纳托利亚的低收入迁入者、失业者等，作为租客或占居者搬入塔尔拉巴舍低标准的住宅，其中有些已被遗弃”（Akbulut 1995，219）。M. 里法特·阿克布卢特补充，建筑的破败、贝伊奥卢夜生活从业者的迁入，以及当地的非法活动，使塔尔拉巴舍陷入“彻底衰败”，并引起公众不安（219）。作为将塔尔拉巴舍街改建为林荫大道的“整治”项目的一部分，1986至1988年，这一区域实施了规模巨大、争议重重的拆除计划。共368栋建筑被拆，其中167栋登记为历史遗产（219）。
en: Tarlabaşı, an area near the Grand Rue de Péra, was a place where almost only minorities dwelled and ran businesses until the 1930s when Muslim families started to move in.

In the 1940s, there was an increase in the number of Muslims moving into the area; yet, in this period, Pera and Tarlabaşı were still dominated by minorities and Levantines. However, with the implementation of the Wealth Tax (1942–1943), a significant amount of business and property was transferred from them to the Muslim population.

With the Riots of 6–7 September 1955, many non-Muslim inhabitants of the city, particularly Greeks, left the country, selling some of their properties (Üsdiken 1995, 218). With the enactment of the 1964 Decree, 35,000 to 40,000 Greeks were expelled from Turkey (Demir and Akar 1999, 157–158). Since they had to leave the country within a very short period of time, they could not sell their properties, and eventually these started to be rented to third parties by unauthorised people. These developments had a direct and massive impact on Tarlabaşı: “Especially after the 1960s Tarlabaşı and surroundings became an area inhabited by low income groups due to internal migration and the changes in the property structure. Low-income migrants from Anatolia, the unemployed and so forth started to move in as renters or squatters, into low-standard residences of Tarlabaşı, some of which were abandoned” (Akbulut 1995, 219). M. Rıfat Akbulut adds that the dilapidation of the buildings, the moving in of people working in the nightlife of Beyoğlu, and illegal activities here pushed Tarlabaşı into “complete deterioration” and caused discomfort in public (219). As a result of the ‘rehabilitation’ project to turn Tarlabaşı Street into a boulevard, a massive and controversial demolition programme was implemented in the area in 1986–1988. A total of 368 buildings, 167 of which were registered as historical heritage, were demolished (219).

zh: 1982年3月，麦夫鲁特服完兵役回到伊斯坦布尔，搬进塔尔拉巴舍，租下“一栋老希腊人房子里［……］二层的一间公寓”（197）。有一段描写1987年拆除计划实施期间，他的堂兄弟苏莱曼来访，其中很长一部分是苏莱曼兴致勃勃地解释：1980年军事政变之后，新市长如何将木匠和修理工赶出塔尔拉巴舍、关闭单身汉宿舍，并评论现状：“过去五年，这一带到处都是流浪汉和被遗弃的人，穷乡下人、库尔德人、吉卜赛人和外国人纷纷住进这些街道，街区比十五年前的桑树山还糟。现在只有再来一次政变，才能把这里清理干净”（264）。苏莱曼自己的出身也是乡村迁入者，他的评论却明显歧视少数族群与乡村迁入者。他还补充，在桑树山和灰山一带垄断建筑业的武拉尔控股公司，曾打算低价买下这里几栋珍贵建筑，后来因产权证问题取消计划。他的歧视性话语以一种愿望收尾：用强制、非人道的方式改造街区，而这实际上将服务于资本家的利益。下面这段以间接话语呈现的官员对街区的说法，比苏莱曼的歧视言辞还要严厉。这里不仅是歧视，更是为拆除提供正当理由的污名化：
en: In March 1982, Mevlut comes back to Istanbul upon completing his military service and moves to Tarlabaşı, renting “a second-floor apartment [...] in an old Greek house” (197). In a passage depicting his cousin Süleyman’s visit to him at his place, in 1987 during the demolition programme, there is a long section where Süleyman explains, with great enthusiasm, how following the 1980 military coup, the new mayor pushed carpenters and mechanics out of Tarlabaşı and shut down the bachelor dormitories, and comments on the current situation: “In the last five years, this whole place has been overrun by drifters and castaways, and there are so many poor rural migrants, Kurds, Gypsies, and foreigners who have settled on these streets that the neighbourhood is worse than Duttepe was fifteen years ago. Only another coup could clean this place up now” (264). In Süleyman’s comments, discrimination against ethnic minorities and rural migrants is clear, although he is also a rural migrant. Süleyman also adds that the Vural Holdings, the building firm which has a monopoly in the Duttepe and Kültepe area, has attempted to purchase a couple of precious buildings here for a low price, but then cancelled the plan because of title deed problems. His discriminatory discourse concludes with a wish for a forceful, inhumane transformation of the neighbourhood which will, as a matter of fact, serve capitalist interests. The argument of the public officials about the neighbourhood, given as indirect discourse, in the excerpt below, is even harsher than Süleyman’s discriminatory words. Here, the case is not only discrimination but also stigmatisation that justifies the demolition:

zh: 拆除计划被宣布为一项清理城市、使其现代化的努力，这种说法吸引了所有人。目前占住街区空置建筑的罪犯、库尔德人、吉卜赛人和小偷将被赶走；毒窟、走私者的仓库、妓院、单身汉宿舍，以及充当非法活动中心的破败建筑，都将被拆除，取而代之的是一条新的六车道公路，让你五分钟就能从泰佩巴舍到塔克西姆。（317）
en: The program of demolitions was announced as an effort to clean up and modernise the city, an approach that appealed to everyone. Criminals, Kurds Gypsies, and thieves currently squatting in the neighbourhood’s vacant buildings would get kicked out; drug dens, smugglers’ warehouses, brothels, bachelor dormitories, and ruined buildings that served as hubs of illegal activities would be demolished, and in their place would be a new six-lane highway taking you from Tepebaşı to Taksim in five minutes. (317)

zh: 叙述者对塔尔拉巴舍的看法是中性的。在第十二章靠前的一段，他这样描述街区的情形：
en: The narrator’s viewpoint about Tarlabaşı is neutral. In an early paragraph in the twelfth chapter, he describes the situation in the neighbourhood as follows:

zh: 随着土耳其东部冲突愈演愈烈，麦夫鲁特看着库尔德迁入者一家又一家地填满塔尔拉巴舍的街道。这些新来者都是强硬的人，完全不像随和的费尔哈特。他们的村庄在战争中被清空、烧成平地。他们很穷，从不买钵扎，所以麦夫鲁特很少去他们的街区。后来，毒贩和无家可归、吸胶的年轻人开始频繁出入这一带，他就完全不去了。（310）
en: As the conflict in Eastern Turkey grew more violent, Mevlut watched the streets of Tarlabaşı fill up, one family at a time, with Kurdish migrants. These newcomers were tough people, nothing like easy-going Ferhat. Their villages had been evacuated and burned to the ground during the war. They were poor and never bought any boza, so Mevlut rarely went to their neighbourhoods. He stopped going altogether when drug dealers and homeless, glue-sniffing young men began to frequent the area. (310)

zh: 这里或许有必要解释一个历史细节。以上引文出自以1987年为背景的段落，即1988年塔尔拉巴舍大道开通之前不久。然而，村庄遭官方下令焚烧的库尔德家庭，是近十年后、20世纪90年代中期才迁往伊斯坦布尔的。因此，引文中这一看似混淆之处，可能是作者有意将塔尔拉巴舍不同时期的氛围交织，也可能只是帕慕克忽略了这一历史事实。上述引文中，叙述者先描述库尔德人来到塔尔拉巴舍，随后提到街区中的毒贩和被排斥者。这现实地描绘了当地处境：贫困居民因为只负担得起这里，才住在这里，却不得不应对与危险人物共处的困难。
en: It might be useful to explain a historical detail here. The excerpts above are taken from the passage set in 1987, shortly before the opening of the Tarlabaşı Boulevard in 1988. However, Kurdish families whose villages were set on fire by official orders migrated to Istanbul almost a decade later, in the mid-1990s. So, this seeming confusion in the excerpt might be an authorial decision to enmesh the atmospheres of Tarlabaşı in different periods, or Pamuk might have simply overlooked this historical fact. In the quote above, the narrator first describes the Kurds’ arrival in Tarlabaşı then mentions the existence of drug dealers and outcasts in the neighbourhood. This is a realistic illustration of the place where poor dwellers of the neighbourhood, who live there because this is all they can afford, have to cope with the difficulties of being around dangerous people.

zh: 书中稍后，到了20世纪90年代，费尔哈特告诉麦夫鲁特：“除非有枪，否则这个街区已经没法住了”，并补充：“毒品、妓女、异装者，各种帮派”（442—443）。费尔哈特是阿列维派，他的评论并不建立在族群和／或教派偏见上；他只是观察街区的危险，并没有希望用铁腕改变这里。他可能夸大了情况，也可能没有，这完全取决于他指的是塔尔拉巴舍的哪些街巷。公众对这一区域的看法，通过这样的评论进入小说。
en: At a later point in the book, in the 1990s Ferhat tells Mevlut: “you can’t live in this neighbourhood anymore unless you’ve got a gun” and adds: “drugs, prostitutes, transvestites, all kinds of gangs” (442–443). The comments of Ferhat, who is an Alevi, are not based on ethnic and/or sectarian prejudice; he simply observes the dangers in the neighbourhood, without wishing for an iron fist to change it. He may or may not be exaggerating the situation, this entirely depends on which streets and alleys of Tarlabaşı he refers to. The public perception about the area enters the book through such comments.

zh: 临近小说结尾，21世纪初，在大规模塔尔拉巴舍城市改造项目启动前约十年，街区中开始流传有关这一计划的传言。此时，叙述者解释，麦夫鲁特在塔尔拉巴舍一直觉得自己是局外人，而如今当地的新变化，使这种感觉更强烈。他现实地描写街区不断衰败的过程：“那些受亚美尼亚人和希腊人训练的老木匠、铁匠、修理工和店主全都走了，那些为了生存愿意干任何活的勤劳家庭也走了，现在连亚述人也走了，取而代之的是毒贩、搬入废弃公寓的迁入者、无家可归者、匪徒和皮条客”（524）。这段解释之后，叙述者以中性语调介绍街区帮派兴起的情况，体现了客观立场。
en: Towards the end of the novel, in the early 2000s, about a decade before the start of the massive Tarlabaşı urban transformation project, rumours about this plan pervade the neighbourhood. At this point, the narrator explains that Mevlut has always felt like an outsider in Tarlabaşı, and now, with the recent changes in the place, this feeling grows stronger. He realistically describes the downward spiral in the neighbourhood: “the old carpenters, blacksmiths, repairmen, and shopkeepers trained by the Armenians and the Greeks had all left, as had those hardworking families ready to do any job to survive, and now the Assyrians were also gone, replaced by drug dealers, migrants moving into abandoned apartments, homeless people, gangsters, and pimps” (524). After this explanation the narrator gives information on the rise of gangs in the neighbourhood through a neutral tone reflecting an objective stance.

zh: 小说中，帕慕克对塔尔拉巴舍的总体处理，反对污名化话语。他强调，这个街区过去和现在确实有人从事轻微或严重的非法活动。然而，大多数居民与这种生活方式无关，只是在城市里努力生存的穷人。他还使人们注意到，资本家在街区两次改造行动中获得的利益，以及污名化话语如何被用作使这些行动正当化的工具。
en: In the novel, Pamuk’s general approach to Tarlabaşı is against a stigmatising discourse. He stresses that there were and are those engaged in minor or major illegal activities in this neighbourhood. However, most of the inhabitants of the place have nothing to do with such a lifestyle, just the poor trying to survive in the city. He also draws attention to the benefits of capitalists in the two transformation operations in the neighbourhood, and that the stigmatising discourse is employed as a vehicle for legitimising these operations.

zh: 加齐是作品中另一个具有强烈存在感的街区，帕慕克将其虚构化的方式，值得讨论。如前所述，小说纳入许多历史事件，并忠实遵循历史资料。帕慕克在一次访谈中解释：“小说讲述了土耳其，尤其是伊斯坦布尔，过去四十年的转型”（转引自Parla 2015，121）。在这样一部类似编年史的小说中，灰山和桑树山这两个棚户区却是虚构的，令人惊讶。然而，灰山（Kül
）与桑树山（Dut
），再现的是同样位于梅吉迪耶柯伊和津吉尔利库尤附近的库什泰佩（鸟山）、居尔泰佩（玫瑰山）等街区；名称中的“山”（
），显然公然指向这些真实街区。杰拉尔认为，帕慕克为这些现实主义描绘的棚户区取虚构名字，也许只是为了避免人们讨论它们与现实是否精确吻合（2015，10）。然而，加齐在小说中出现时，情况很特别。加齐是一个真实街区，在书中却以半虚构方式呈现。在讨论这样做的结果之前，不妨先简要介绍加齐这个伊斯坦布尔边缘街区。
en: Gazi, another neighbourhood with a solid presence in the work, is worthy of discussion in the way Pamuk fictionalises it. As mentioned earlier, the novel includes numerous events from history adhering faithfully to historical data. In an interview, Pamuk explains that “in the novel Turkey’s, particularly Istanbul’s transformation in the last forty years is told” (quoted in Parla 2015, 121). The fact that the shanty towns of Kültepe and Duttepe are fictional is surprising in a novel which resembles a chronicle. However, Kültepe (Ash Hill) and Duttepe (Mulberry Hill) are representations of neighbourhoods such as Kuştepe (Bird Hill) and Gültepe (Rose Hill), similarly located near Mecidiyeköy and Zincirlikuyu, and obviously the hill (

) in their names is an open reference to these factual neighbourhoods. Celal argues that Pamuk’s decision to give fictional names to these realistically depicted shanty towns might be simply because he did not want to encounter discussions of precise compatibility with reality (2015, 10). However, when it comes to the appearance of Gazi in the novel, the situation is unique. In the book, Gazi, a factual neighbourhood, appears semi-fictionally. Before discussing the results of this, it might be useful to give brief information about Gazi, a periphery neighbourhood of Istanbul.

zh: 让-弗朗索瓦·佩鲁兹指出，围绕加齐街区，存在以“灾难论”和“耸人听闻”为基础的“神话”（2011，72）。他认为，这套神话有三个主要构成：加齐是阿列维派街区、左翼街区和库尔德街区（73）。佩鲁兹强调，在这种框架下，“加齐是一个危险的［……］‘被污名化’的街区”（73）；他补充，1995年3月的事件强化了这种看法（73—74）。

依据在户籍登记档案中的研究及当地田野调查，佩鲁兹指出，加齐并不是库尔德街区（82）。他又说，虽然阿列维派占多数，但加齐也有相当数量的逊尼派人口（85）。基于同居民的谈话，他强调，“加齐既不能被称为‘左翼街区’”，也不能被称为“解放区”，因为大多数居民远谈不上支持武装激进左翼团体（91）。不过，他认为，在1995年事件前后，警方持续对加齐施加的心理刺激，导致了一种“由共同‘受压迫’感而生的差异意识”（92）。
en: Jean-François Pérouse acknowledges the “mythology” about the Gazi Neighbourhood based on “catastrophism” and “sensationalism” (2011, 72). He asserts that this mythology has three main constituents: Gazi is an Alevi, leftist and Kurdish neighbourhood (73). Pérouse stresses that within such a framework, “Gazi is a dangerous [...] ‘stigmatised’ neighbourhood” (73), and adds that the events in March 1995 contributed to this perception of it (73–74).

Depending on his research in the register office archives as well as his fieldwork in the area, Pérouse observes that Gazi is not a Kurdish neighbourhood (82). He adds that, although Alevis are the majority, there is a considerable Sunni population in Gazi (85). From his conversations with Gazi inhabitants, he emphasises that “Gazi can neither be described as a ‘leftist neighbourhood’” nor as a “liberated area”, as the majority of the residents are far from supporting the armed radical leftist groups (91). However, he asserts that constant psychological agitation by the police in Gazi, both before and after the events of 1995, led to a “consciousness of difference stemming from a mutual feeling of ‘oppression’” (92).

zh: 作品中的加齐，是加齐街区与伊斯坦布尔另一个街区1 Mayıs Mahallesi（五一街区）的混合体。正如许克吕·阿斯兰详细解释的，五一街区是在20世纪70年代后半期，由左翼团体领导建立的（2004，87—115）。小说将它的故事移到了加齐名下。这一替换引出两个重要问题：为什么这样做？它对小说总体表达有什么影响？
en: The Gazi that appears in the work is an amalgam of the Gazi Neighbourhood and another neighbourhood in Istanbul called the 1 Mayıs Mahallesi (1st of May Neighbourhood). As Şükrü Aslan explains in detail, the 1st of May Neighbourhood was established under the leadership of leftist groups in the second half of the 1970s (2004, 87–115). Its story is attributed to Gazi in the novel. This substitution raises two important issues: What is the reason for it? What is its effect on the overall message of the novel?

zh: 帕慕克在一次访谈中说明，为了费尔哈特的故事，加齐街区是他为写这本书进行调研时走访的地方之一（Pamuk 2014c，23）。第四部第九章题为“加齐街区”（274），其中有一大段讲述街区如何建立。然而，真实的加齐并非如此建立；这一章中的建区故事，属于五一街区。在另一次访谈中，被问及小说里的加齐故事是否属实时，帕慕克这样回答：“是的，但这是五一街区的故事。那里曾发生过某种社会主义起义。”（Pamuk 2014b）。
en: In an interview, Pamuk clarifies that, in connection with Ferhat’s story, the Gazi Neighbourhood was one of the places he visited during his research for the book (Pamuk 2014c, 23). In Part IV, in Chapter 9 entitled “The Ghaazi [Gazi] Quarter” (274), we read a lengthy passage on the establishment of the neighbourhood. However, factually Gazi was not established in this way; the establishment story included in the chapter belongs to the 1st of May Neighbourhood. In another interview, Pamuk replies as follows when asked whether the story of Gazi in the novel is true: “Yes, but this is the story of 1st of May Neighbourhood. There had happened a sort of a socialist uprising.” (Pamuk 2014b).

zh: 简单说，帕慕克在小说中将加齐和五一街区的身份结合起来，创造出一个虚构的加齐。在一部相当忠于历史事实的作品中，这会造成混淆。有趣的是，帕慕克虚构加齐的方式，与佩鲁兹所描述的这一街区的神话非常吻合：它是库尔德、阿列维派和左翼的街区。极有可能，大多数读者不会核查书中加齐的故事究竟是事实还是虚构。他们很可能以为故事建立在历史事实之上。因此，帕慕克也许无意间参与了对被污名化的加齐街区的神话的再生产。
en: Put simply, Pamuk combines the identities of the Gazi and 1st of May Neighbourhoods in the novel to create a fictional Gazi. This causes confusion in a work which is rather faithful to historical facts. Interestingly, the way Pamuk fictionalises Gazi in the novel is very much in line with what Pérouse describes as the mythologies about this neighbourhood: that it is a Kurdish, Alevi and left-wing neighbourhood. Most probably, the majority of the book’s readers will not check whether the story of Gazi in the book is factual or fictional. It is very likely that they will assume it is based on historical facts. Consequently, Pamuk, probably unintentionally, contributes to the reproduction of the mythologies about the stigmatised neighbourhood of Gazi.

zh: 城市中的男人与女人
en: Men and Women in the City

zh: 帕慕克没有将迁移经验的性别维度作为问题深入展开。在麦夫鲁特这个从安纳托利亚村庄来到伊斯坦布尔的年轻男子的发展过程中，这一倾向尤其引人注意。麦夫鲁特大约二十岁时，爱上一个在街上不断遇见的女人；帕慕克浅略地触及了他对性别问题的看法的变化。他给这个女人取名奈丽曼，过了一阵便开始跟踪她。在叙述者通过自由间接话语传达麦夫鲁特对此的想法的一段中，我们观察到他的性别观念发生了变化。这里，麦夫鲁特设想，假如在村里，他的姐妹也被一个男人跟踪，就像他现在跟踪奈丽曼一样，会是什么情形。他承认自己会感到愤怒，却不认为自己的行为存在道德问题，因为“伊斯坦布尔不是村庄”（106）。在这里，帕慕克只是暗示麦夫鲁特意识到了乡村与城市在性别问题上的根本区别。然而，他没有再往前一步，让麦夫鲁特追问：如果
，有男人在街上跟踪自己的姐妹，他会作何反应。
en: Pamuk refrains from problematising the gender aspect of the migration experience. This tendency attracts attention, particularly in Mevlut’s development, who comes to Istanbul as a young man from a village in Anatolia. Pamuk superficially addresses the changes in Mevlut’s perception of gender issues when he, around the age of twenty, falls in love with a woman he keeps encountering in the street. He names this woman Neriman, and after a while starts following her. In a passage where the narrator conveys Mevlut’s thoughts on this, via free indirect discourse, we observe the changes in his mentality as regards gender issues. Here, Mevlut imagines a scenario where his sisters were followed by a man in the village, the way he is following Neriman right now. While he accepts that he would feel rage about this, he does not find a moral problem with his own act since “Istanbul was not a village” (106). Here, Pamuk confines himself to imply Mevlut’s awareness of the fundamental differences between the country and the city as regards gender issues. Yet, he does not take the next step of making Mevlut question how he would react if a man
followed his sisters on the street.

zh: 帕慕克并未明确展示麦夫鲁特在性别问题上进步到什么程度，但我们可以推知，他至少比乡村观念前进了一步。例如，他赞赏女儿在城市中与人交往时的自在。不过，麦夫鲁特从未鼓励妻子拉伊哈参与城市生活。拉伊哈既不独自、也不与丈夫一起走入公共领域；她总待在家里，身处家庭的、私人的领域。麦夫鲁特的女儿们作为第二代迁入女性，同城市的联系远比母亲多。
en: While Pamuk does not explicitly demonstrate the extent of Mevlut’s progress on gender issues, we can infer that he is at least a step further on than rural perceptions, for instance, when he admires his daughter for her relaxedness when socialising in the city. That said, Mevlut never encourages his wife Rayiha to be a part of urban life. Rayiha is not out in the public sphere, alone or with her husband; she is always at home, in the domestic, private sphere. Mevlut’s daughters, as second-generation migrant women, have much more connection with the city than their mother has.

zh: 帕慕克把拉伊哈描绘成一个与家庭以外生活脱节的女人，同时强调她的姐妹，尤其萨米哈，对城市的喜爱。事实上，一个重要细节是：除麦夫鲁特外，对城市怀有强烈积极情感的，只有这两个女人，而没有任何男人。萨米哈这样解释自己的感受：“人群、躲着公共汽车跑到马路对面的人、穿裙子的女孩、马车、公园、高大的老公寓楼；这一切我都喜欢”（252）。萨米哈的话，尤其是她把老公寓楼也包括在内，呼应了城市作为
的观念，值得注意。她描述自己如何、为何热爱城市，也反映出她渴望作为女人在城市中得到解放，挑战男人对穿什么、怎么行动的霸权。自由感是她依恋城市的重要原因。事实上，在土耳其语原文中，她说自己喜欢“
etek giyen kızları”（
穿裙子的女孩）（Pamuk 2014a，208）；上引英译只译作“穿裙子的女孩”（2015，252），丢失了这一细微意味。

同费尔哈特结婚后，萨米哈到市中心的公寓里做家政工，喜欢待在伊斯坦布尔中心地区。与麦夫鲁特一样，她觉得城市会对她说话（237）。她羡慕费尔哈特在卡拉柯伊长大：“想到费尔哈特在卡拉柯伊、就在城市正中心度过童年，真是美好；回家后，我会请他给我讲那些日子”（289）。维迪哈是三姐妹中的长姐，嫁给了科尔库特，也喜欢在城中走动。苏莱曼描述他们为了他的婚事去相看合适女孩时提到：“维迪哈太喜欢出门了”（299）。维迪哈解释，为科尔库特相看人选，是她获得丈夫许可、到城里去的最容易的办法（300）。最后，科尔库特与一个女歌手交往，但家里不同意。除这些小片段之外，帕慕克没有处理迁入者城市生活的性别维度。
en: While Pamuk portrays Rayiha as a woman disconnected from life outside home, he emphasises her sisters’, particularly Samiha’s, admiration for the city. In fact, it is an important detail that these two women, rather than any men, are the only characters, apart from Mevlut, with strong positive feelings for the city. Samiha explains hers as follows: “the crowds, the people dodging buses as they run to the other side of the road, the girls in skirts, the horse-drawn carts, the parks, the big old apartment buildings; I love it all” (252). The resonance of the city as

in Samiha’s words, especially in her inclusion of old apartment buildings, is worthy of notice. The way she describes how and why she loves the city also reflects her desire to be liberated as a woman in the city, challenging the male hegemony on what to wear and how to behave. The feeling of freedom is an important reason for her attachment to the city. In fact, in the Turkish original, she says she likes “
etek giyen kızları” (girls wearing skirts
) (Pamuk 2014a, 208), a nuance lost in the translation above which simply renders it as “the girls in skirts” (2015, 252).

After marrying Ferhat, Samiha works as a domestic worker in apartments in the city centre, and enjoys being in central areas of Istanbul. Like Mevlut, she thinks that the city talks to her (237). She admires Ferhat for having grown up in Karaköy: “it was nice to think that Ferhat had spent his childhood in Karaköy, right in the middle of the city, and when I got home I would ask him to tell me about those days” (289). Vediha, the oldest of the three sisters who is married to Korkut, also loves travelling in the city, as mentioned by Süleyman when he describes their visits to seek out eligible girls for his marriage: “Vediha loved being out of the house so much” (299). Vediha explains that visiting candidates for Korkut is the easiest way for her to get permission from her husband to go out in the city (300). Eventually, Korkut has a relationship with a singer woman, but his family does not approve of this. Other than these minor instances Pamuk does not address the gender dimension of migrants’ life in the city.
body.review: 此段先说维迪哈已嫁给科尔库特（Korkut），且相看女孩是为苏莱曼（Süleyman）的婚事，随后却写为科尔库特相看人选、科尔库特与女歌手交往。人名照底本保留，不擅自替换。

zh: 结论
en: Conclusion

zh: 《我脑袋里的怪东西》的时间跨度约为四十年：从麦夫鲁特1969年迁往伊斯坦布尔，到2012年。在此期间发生于伊斯坦布尔的变化，对小说场景及多个主题的处理都具有重要意义。小说较早处，有一长段写麦夫鲁特在城中生活二十五年后，如何感知城市变化。叙述者从街道与房屋的变化写起，谈到人时，作出如下评论：“过去街上那些穿着灰暗衣服、安静而受压抑的人，被喧闹、精力旺盛、更加自信强硬的人群取代了”（19）。这一描写，与下面引述的麦夫鲁特对新迁入者的想法一起，表现出好迁入者与坏迁入者的对立：过去通情达理的好迁入者，与如今令人畏惧的坏迁入者相对照。
en: is a novel set within a timespan of about forty years: from 1969, when Mevlut migrates to Istanbul, to 2012. The changes that took place in Istanbul in that period of time have significance in relation to the setting as well as to the treatment of various themes in the book. Early in the novel, there is a long passage on Mevlut’s perception of the changes in the city after he has spent twenty-five years there. The narrator begins with the changing streets and houses, and when it comes to people, he makes the following comment: “the quiet, brownbeaten folk in gray and drab clothes who used to populate the streets had been replaced by rowdy, energetic, and more assertive crowds” (19). This depiction, together with Mevlut’s thoughts on the new migrants of the city quoted below, appear as an expression of the good migrant–bad migrant opposition: reasonable good migrants of the past as opposed to the intimidating bad migrants of the present.
body.review: 本章开篇将小说时段概括为20世纪70年代初至21世纪头十年末；此处则明确写1969—2012年。两处均按底本保留。

zh: 很长一段时间，麦夫鲁特欢迎城市中的新事物：“他不把城市看作一个在自己到来之前就已存在、而自己以局外人身份进入的地方。相反，他喜欢想象，伊斯坦布尔是在自己生活其中时建成的，梦想它未来会更干净、更美、更现代”（318）。感到自己是这些变化的一部分，强化了麦夫鲁特对城市的依恋，以及作为城市一员的身份。然而，随着小说展开，他对此的看法开始改变，转向相反的方向。他在周围观察到的差异，使他不安：“城市不再是一个巨大、熟悉的家，而是一个无情无信的空间，谁有机会，谁就再添更多混凝土、街道、院落、墙壁、人行道和商店”（509）。
en: For a long time, Mevlut welcomes the new in the city: “He didn’t see the city as a place that had existed before his arrival and to which he’d come as an outsider. Instead, he liked to imagine that Istanbul was being built while he lived in it and to dream of how much cleaner, more beautiful, and more modern it would be in the future” (318). Feeling himself a part of these changes strengthens Mevlut’s attachment to the city and his identity as a member of it. However, as the novel proceeds, his views on that start to alter and evolve toward the opposite direction. The differences he observes all around leads to unsettling feelings in him: “the city was no longer an enormous, familiar home but a faithless space in which anyone who got the chance added more concrete, more streets, courtyards, walls, pavements, and shops” (509).

zh: 帕慕克在“新街区，老面孔”一章（517），讨论麦夫鲁特对21世纪初塔尔拉巴舍变化的不适，这促使他决定搬离。塔尔拉巴舍的帮派、贩毒和卖淫活动日益增多，愈发显眼，让麦夫鲁特感到忧惧。无论来自本国还是外国，他都不喜欢街区的新居民。他观察到外国人——大多是过境移民——数量增加，对街区的理解也变了：“如今，他逐渐习惯把塔尔拉巴舍看作许多漫长旅程中一个暂时停靠的站点”（526）。街区中越来越多的街头摊位也令他恼火；他不喜欢经营这些摊位的新街头小贩。
en: Pamuk addresses Mevlut’s discomfort about the changes in Tarlabaşı at the beginning of the 2000s, which leads to his decision to move out, in the chapter entitled “New Quarters, Old Faces” (517). Mevlut feels apprehension with the increasing presence and visibility of gangs, drug dealing and prostitution in Tarlabaşı. He is displeased with the new inhabitants of the neighbourhood, be they natives or foreigners. As he observes the rise in the number of foreigners, most of whom are transit migrants, his perception of the neighbourhood alters: “by now he was getting used to the idea of Tarlabaşı as just a temporary stop on so many longer journeys” (526). He is also irritated by the increasing number of street stalls in the neighbourhood, and he does not like the new street vendors running them.

zh: 麦夫鲁特不适的某些方面，说明每一代迁入者如何把下一批新来者看作局外人。换言之，早来的迁入者觉得自己有权生活在城市，却往往不愿将这一权利“授予”后来者。麦夫鲁特住在直接受迁移影响的塔尔拉巴舍，因此较早地从内部见证了城市在迁入人口及相关社会动态方面的变化。在一处自由间接话语中，我们听到麦夫鲁特对伊斯坦布尔新迁入者的想法：“伊斯坦布尔到处都是用手提箱走私违禁品的乌克兰女人、非洲移民，以及把人榨干的阴险掮客；城市成了腐败与贿赂的温床”（395）。虽然这句话重点在外国人，但土耳其语的“çeşit tuhaf insan”（各种各样的怪人）（Pamuk 2014a，322），在英译中变成了“阴险掮客”，显然原词涵盖所有新来者，无论外国还是本国。在这样的评论中，叙述者与麦夫鲁特之间的界线含混。麦夫鲁特看待城市新居民的方式，类似较早几十年伊斯坦布尔人看待迁入者的方式；那时，麦夫鲁特等许多人刚来到这里。引文之后的心理叙述，突出新旧迁入者之间的分野。麦夫鲁特注意到“一类新的穷人”（481），他们在街上捡垃圾，而这些街道“变化［……］太快。文字太多，人太多，噪音太多”（481）。他也辨认出“一类更强硬、更愤怒的新小贩”（481）。他悲伤地目睹“老一代街头小贩被城市的喧嚣吞没了”（481）。在麦夫鲁特所观察的全球化的伊斯坦布尔中，迁入者向上流动的可能，比前几十年更小；这一事实使他们在城市中的挣扎几乎带有攻击性。
en: Some aspects of Mevlut’s discomfort illustrates how each generation of migrants sees the next newcomers as outsiders. In other words, while former migrants feel the right to live in the city, they tend not to ‘grant’ migrants who come after them this right. As Mevlut lives in Tarlabaşı, a neighbourhood directly affected by migration, he becomes an early and insider witness of the changes in the city as regards the migrant population and related social dynamics. In a free indirect discourse, we hear what Mevlut thinks about the new migrants in Istanbul: “Istanbul was crawling with Ukrainian women smuggling contraband in their suitcases, African migrants, and shady operators who sucked people dry; the city had become a hotbed of corruption and bribery” (395). Although the focus in this sentence is foreigners, the expression “çeşit tuhaf insan” (all sorts of strange people) (Pamuk 2014a, 322) which appears in the English translation as “shady operators”, obviously includes all newcomers, foreign or native. In comments like this, the boundary between the narrator and Mevlut is vague. The way Mevlut views these new inhabitants of the city is similar to the way Istanbulites viewed migrants in former decades, when many of them, such as Mevlut, first arrived in the city. The psycho-narration following the above quote accents the divide between the old and the new migrants. Mevlut notices “a new category of poor people” (481), who picked up the rubbish on streets which were “changing [...] very fast. There were too many words and letters, too many people, too much noise” (481). He also identifies “a new class of tougher, angrier hawkers” (481). He sadly witnesses that “the older generation of street vendors had been swallowed up in the tumult of the city” (481). In the globalising Istanbul which Mevlut observes, migrants’ upward mobility is less likely than it was in the earlier decades; a fact that makes them almost aggressive in their struggle in the city.

zh: 改变城市面貌的城市改造，直接影响麦夫鲁特的生活。此时是21世纪初，塔尔拉巴舍城市改造项目即将宣布之前。麦夫鲁特担心房租上涨，觉得塔尔拉巴舍一天比一天难以安居：“他还怀疑，这些匪徒般的人——他那些所谓的房东（每五六年就换一批）——可能突然退出，把房子交给房地产经纪人、房产投机者、急着造酒店的开发商，或者别的帮派，就像过去两年在别处发生的那样”（525）。他观察到塔尔拉巴舍如何成为创造经济租金的焦点，即不进行生产性投资而攫取投机收益：“被忽视了这么多年之后，整个街区突然像磁铁一样，吸来了这座城市能聚集起的所有苦难与破坏性的欲望”（525）。这些都是对塔尔拉巴舍情形完全现实的描写，呈现了生活在贫困街区、被经济租金创造盯上的迁入者的脆弱处境。这一点与城市权利密切相关，因为城市改造项目会侵害居民权利。《我脑袋里的怪东西》暗示塔尔拉巴舍城市改造迫在眉睫，却没有提及其实施。
en: The urban transformation changing the face of the city has direct influences on Mevlut’s life. These are the early 2000s, just before the Tarlabaşı urban transformation project was announced. Mevlut is concerned about the increasing rent. He feels that Tarlabaşı is becoming a more and more awkward place with each passing day: “he also suspected that these gangsterish types – his so-called landlords (who changed every five or six years) – might suddenly pull out and leave the house to real-estate brokers, property speculators, developers eager to build hotels, or to some other gang, as had happened elsewhere over the past two years” (525). He observes how Tarlabaşı becomes a focus of economic rent creation (i.e., capturing speculative gains without any productive investment): “after having been largely ignored for so many years, the whole neighbourhood had suddenly become a magnet for all the misery and destructive appetite that the city could muster” (525). These are all entirely realistic depictions of the situation in Tarlabaşı, portraying the vulnerability of migrants living in poor neighbourhoods, targeted by economic rent creation. This point is closely connected with the right to the city, as urban transformation projects result in violations of inhabitants’ rights. In
, Tarlabaşı’s approaching urban transformation is implied to be imminent but its implementation is not mentioned.

zh: 在城市改造背景下，桑树山与灰山经历的过程，是关于麦夫鲁特如何感受城市变化的另一重要母题。临近全书结尾，我们跟随他走向灰山。他穿行于取代棚屋的公寓楼之间；多年间非法加盖的楼层，使它们愈发丑陋。叙述声音描写它们时，语调明显负面：“丑陋的
，高达六七层”（555）。接下来一段，写麦夫鲁特对城市惊人增长的思考：
en: The process in Duttepe and Kültepe in the context of urban transformation is another important motif in relation to Mevlut’s feelings about the changes in the city. Towards the end of the book, we follow him on his way to Kültepe. He walks through apartment blocks that replaced former shanties, with their unlicensed storeys added over the years, making them all the more ugly. The tone of the narrative voice is clearly negative in its description: “hideous
homes, six or seven stories high” (555). The passage continues with a paragraph of Mevlut’s thoughts on the incredible growth of the city:

zh: 在与拉伊哈婚后那些幸福的岁月里［……］，他一直以为伊斯坦布尔永远不会变，以为自己在街头辛苦劳作，总有一天会换来一处属于自己的地方。这一切在某种程度上都实现了。但过去四十年，另有一千万人和他一样来到了伊斯坦布尔，和他一样，能抓住什么就抓住什么，而城市也因此面目全非。麦夫鲁特初到时，伊斯坦布尔人口只有三百万；现在，据说有一千三百万人住在那里。（556）
en: Throughout the happy years of his marriage to Rayiha [...] he’d always thought that Istanbul would never change, that all his hard work out on the streets would gain him a place of his own someday. All this had happened, to an extent. But ten million other people had joined him in Istanbul over the past forty years, latching on as he had to anything they could find, and the city had emerged transformed. Istanbul’s population had been only three million when Mevlut had first arrived; now, they said there were thirteen million people living there. (556)

zh: 小说倒数第二章结束于一阵淹没麦夫鲁特的怀旧之情：他看着自己长大的棚屋被拆除，武拉尔控股公司将在原地建起公寓楼。
en: This penultimate chapter of the novel ends with a wave of nostalgia that engulfs Mevlut as he watches the shanty he grew up in be demolished, to be replaced with an apartment building by Vural Holdings.

zh: 麦夫鲁特对城市的疏离感，处于最后一章、因而也处于小说结尾的中心。他反思自己的感受，试图找到原因：“是因为那股势不可挡、不断膨胀的洪流，因为数以百万计的新来者涌入伊斯坦布尔，把新房子、摩天楼和购物中心带来了吗？［麦夫鲁特］开始看到［……］被拆除的不只是贫困街区摇摇欲坠的房子，甚至还有塔克西姆和希什利那些存在了四十多年的像样建筑”（574）。他想到老建筑及其居民：“随着那些老人同他们建造的房子一起消失，新人搬进新楼——楼比以往更高、更可怕，混凝土更多。每当望着这些三四十层的新塔楼，麦夫鲁特就觉得，自己与住在里面的新人毫无关系”（574）。正如这段所表明的，城市变化是新自由主义化，以及伊斯坦布尔作为新兴全球城市的新身份的结果。具有政治关系的精英攫取经济租金、城市改造、城市贫困和国际移民，是这一历史局面的伴随现象。
en: Mevlut’s estrangement from the city is at the centre of the final chapter and, therefore, of the ending of the novel. He reflects on his feelings, trying to find the reasons for them: “Was it because of that unstoppable, swelling flood, the millions of new people coming to Istanbul and bringing new houses, skyscrapers, and shopping malls with them? [Mevlut] began to see [...] demolished not just ramshackle houses in poor neighbourhoods, but even proper buildings in Taksim and Şişli that had stood for over forty years” (574). He thinks about the old buildings and their dwellers: “As those old people disappeared along with the buildings they’d made, new people moved into new buildings – taller, more terrifying, and more concrete than ever before. Whenever he looked at these new thirty- and forty-storey towers, Mevlut felt that he had nothing to do with any of the new people who lived in them” (574). As the passage indicates, the changes in the city are consequences of neoliberalisation and Istanbul’s new identity as an emerging global city. The capture of economic rent by politically connected elites, urban transformation, urban poverty and international migration are concomitants of this historical conjuncture.

zh: 接下来一页，通过一处心理叙述，我们听到麦夫鲁特对伊斯坦布尔新迁入者的想法，与城市景观变化造成的沮丧交织：“一类新的怪人搬进了
［……］。但最新到来的贫困人群大多住在伊斯坦布尔最偏远的地方，甚至远在第二条环城公路以外，连麦夫鲁特也从未踏足”（576）。思考城市贫困之后，他观察到景观正以同社会肌理一样快的速度变化：“更让麦夫鲁特惊讶的，是那些从这些街区像幽灵一样升起的奇怪新建筑，高得从博斯普鲁斯海峡对岸都能看见。麦夫鲁特喜欢远远地望着这些建筑”（576）。这里两次使用“怪”（
）这个形容词，值得注意，因为它也出现在小说标题里。麦夫鲁特脑袋里的怪，似乎与城市及其人群、景观中的怪联系在一起。
en: On the following page, through an instance of psycho-narration, we hear Mevlut’s thoughts about the new migrants in Istanbul, intertwined with his dismay caused by the city’s changing landscapes: “a new class of strange people had moved into the old

homes [...]. But the newest destitute multitudes mostly lived in the farthest reaches of Istanbul, farther out than the second ring road around the city, where even Mevlut had never set foot” (576). His observations on the landscape that changes as fast as the social fabric follow his thoughts on urban poverty: “What amazed Mevlut even more were the strange new buildings that had begun to rise from these quarters like phantoms, so tall that you could see them from the opposite shore of the Bosporus. Mevlut loved to watch these buildings from afar” (576). The use of the adjective “strange” (

) twice, which is also included in the title of the novel, is noteworthy here. The strangeness in Mevlut’s mind seems to be connected with the strangeness in the city with its people and its landscape.

zh: 麦夫鲁特思考这一切的地点，是堂兄弟苏莱曼在灰山高楼顶层的公寓。武拉尔控股公司在麦夫鲁特的棚屋地块上建起这栋楼；作为交换，他得到楼内一套公寓。堂兄弟科尔库特和苏莱曼也与各自家人住在这栋楼里。那天夜里，三位堂兄弟与妻子们一起吃晚饭。饭后，麦夫鲁特坐到阳台上赏景，书中这样描写这一刻：“一时间他有些眩晕，既因为高度，也因为眼前景观的辽阔”（577）。他凝望楼宇，回想周围山丘的过去：如今城市看上去变化极大，四周建筑的巨大数量令他震惊。眼前景色引起复杂情感：“伊斯坦布尔仍能使他退缩，但即使如今已五十五岁，他仍冲动地想跳入这片凝视着他的建筑森林”（578）。在阳台观景的几分钟，变成了沉思的时刻，使他能够说清自己热爱卖钵扎背后的原因：“夜间在城中行走，让他觉得仿佛在自己的脑袋里漫游”（579）。随后，他出去卖钵扎。
en: The location where Mevlut thinks about all these is his cousin Süleyman’s top floor apartment in the tower block in Kültepe. This was built by Vural Holdings on Mevlut’s shanty’s land; in return he got an apartment in the building. His cousins Korkut and Süleyman also live in this block with their families. That night the three cousins and their wives have dinner together. Afterwards, Mevlut has a seat on the balcony to enjoy the view, a moment described as follows: “he felt dizzy for a moment, both from the height and the sheer expanse of the landscape before him” (577). As he gazes out over the buildings, he recollects the past of the hills around there: the city looks extremely changed now and the massive number of buildings around shocks him. The view in front of him creates mixed feelings: “Istanbul could still make him flinch, but even now at fifty-five years of age, he still felt the urge to leap right into this forest of staring buildings” (578). The minutes of looking at the view from the balcony turn into a moment of contemplation which enables him to define what lies behind his passion for selling boza: “walking around the city at night made him feel as if he were wandering around inside his own head” (579). Later, he goes out to sell boza.

zh: 叙述者解释，最近麦夫鲁特常在梦中见到拉伊哈，她在一座老宅里，而他打不开那扇门。梦中，他无休止地走在街道上，推开不同宅邸的门，拼命试图走到她身边。叙述者补充，近年来，想象与现实在麦夫鲁特脑中交织。他走在夜色中，开始思考：对
多年来

children: 一直同自己说话的城市

zh: ，他想说些什么。此时，一位顾客叫住他。麦夫鲁特走进楼里，交上钵扎；正要离开时，女顾客赞赏他仍在做这份工作。“我卖钵扎，因为这是我想做的事”（584），麦夫鲁特回答。这句话使女人对他更加亲切：“别放弃，卖钵扎的。别觉得在这些高楼和混凝土之间，努力就没有意义”（584）。麦夫鲁特这样回应：“我要一直卖钵扎，直到世界末日”（584）。他沿街继续行走，“走向金角湾，沿着一条仿佛通往遗忘深处的下坡路”（584），终于找到自己想对城市说的话：“我爱拉伊哈，胜过这个世界上的一切”（584）。小说以这句话结束。
en: The narrator explains that recently Mevlut has been seeing Rayiha in his dreams, in an old mansion, the door of which he cannot open. In these dreams, he walks endlessly in the streets and opens the doors of different mansions desperately trying to reach her. The narrator adds that in recent years imagination had been intermingling with reality in Mevlut’s mind. As he walks in the night’s darkness, he starts thinking what he would like to tell to

for all these years. At that point, a customer hails him. Mevlut goes into the building, hands over the boza, and as he is about to leave, the female customer compliments him for doing his job. “I sell boza because it’s what I want to do” (584), Mevlut replies. These words make the woman even more sympathetic towards him: “Don’t ever give up, boza seller. Don’t ever think there’s no point trying among all these towers and all this concrete” (584). Mevlut replies with the following words: “I will sell boza until the day the world ends” (584). He continues walking along a street “toward the Golden Horn, down a road that felt as if it were descending into oblivion” (584), and finds what he wants to tell to the city: “I have loved Rayiha more than anything in this world” (584). The novel ends with these words.

zh: 书的结尾，麦夫鲁特的疏离感转为对过去梦境般的哀歌。钵扎这一来自过去的传统，作为母题不可避免地为全书从首页到末页带来浓厚怀旧情绪；这不应同精英对乡村迁入者到来之前的城市的怀念相混淆。这里怀念的是消逝的传统与生活方式，它们曾是城市生活的组成部分，城市中的所有成员，无论阶级、地位，都可以分享。结尾几页对钵扎母题的聚焦，强化了这一怀旧氛围。在这些最后的段落中，帕慕克突出了买钵扎这一同卖钵扎一样怀旧的行为：小说最后的对话，不是发生在麦夫鲁特与某位主要人物之间，而是发生在卖钵扎的麦夫鲁特与一个无名的买钵扎者之间。两人几乎用一种特殊的暗语交流，那是对一个几乎消失的伊斯坦布尔的热爱与怀念：在那个伊斯坦布尔，小贩走遍街道，有许多顾客。对于买钵扎的女人，麦夫鲁特提着钵扎篮子的身影，象征城市美好的旧日。“别觉得在这些高楼和混凝土之间，努力就没有意义”（584），她这样对麦夫鲁特说，指的是不断变化的城市景观。以高楼和混凝土为基础的意象，主导了小说最后几页。
en: Mevlut’s feelings of estrangement give way to a dreamlike lament to the past in the ending of the book. The motif of boza, a tradition from the past, inevitably brings a considerable nostalgia to the book, from the first page to the last, which should not be confused with the elitist nostalgia for the city before the arrival of rural migrants. The nostalgia here is for the lost traditions and ways of life that were once components of the urban life, and that could be shared by all members of the city regardless of class and status. The focus on the motif of boza in the closing pages of the book intensifies this nostalgic atmosphere. In these final passages, Pamuk brings the act of buying boza, which is as nostalgic as selling boza, to the fore as the final dialogue in the novel is not between Mevlut and one of the major characters, but between Mevlut the boza seller and an anonymous boza buyer. The two communicate almost in a special code, that of love and nostalgia for an almost lost Istanbul: an Istanbul where vendors would walk around the streets and have many customers. For the woman buying boza, Mevlut with his boza basket is a symbol of the beautiful old days of the city. “Don’t ever think there’s no point trying among all these towers and all this concrete” (584) she tells Mevlut, referring to the changing urban landscape. Imagery based on towers and concrete dominate these last pages of the novel.

zh: 这里还有一个怀旧要素。最后这些段落发生于开斋节之夜。麦夫鲁特站在一位顾客门前，看见一群因节日聚在一起的亲友，正一起喝拉克酒。过去庆祝斋月和开斋节的方式，在土耳其已是一种消逝的传统，也是强烈的怀旧母题。对这一场景以及麦夫鲁特感受的描写，在这方面很重要：“他看到慈爱的姨姑、庄重的父亲、合群健谈的母亲、祖父、祖母，还有不知多少孩子”（583）。这种气氛引出一刻内省：“这些人的幸福使麦夫鲁特快乐。人生来就是为了幸福、诚实和坦荡”（583）。因此，这段怀旧文字以某种乐观情绪收尾。
en: There is one more element of nostalgia here. The timing of these final passages is the night of the Eid holiday. As Mevlut is at one of his customer’s doorstep he sees that a group of family and friends who have come together for the holiday are drinking raki together. The way the Ramadan and Eid holidays were celebrated in the past is a bygone tradition in Turkey, a strong motif of nostalgia. The description of this setting and Mevlut’s feelings about it are important in this regard: “he saw loving aunts, dignified fathers, gregarious mothers, grandfathers, grandmothers, and an indefinite number of children” (583). The atmosphere leads to a moment of introspection: “these people’s happiness pleased Mevlut. Human beings were made to be happy, honest, and open” (583). Thus, the nostalgic passage ends with a degree of optimism.

zh: 麦夫鲁特梦中的意象，是小说结尾强化怀旧的另一个细节。如前所述，他在梦中看见拉伊哈身处一座老宅；这种老宅是风景如画的旧伊斯坦布尔最鲜明的象征之一。梦中他无法抵达她身边，因为走过的街道不断变化。在不断变化、无法找到爱人这两个母题中，可以发现对他所爱、却已大半消逝的伊斯坦布尔的指涉。全书最后一幕的场景，是费里柯伊一带一条通往金角湾的街道。这些街道位于穆斯林街区与昔日少数族群街区的交会点，尚未被城市改造彻底摧毁，仍留有一丝旧伊斯坦布尔的气息。麦夫鲁特的最后一句话，也是小说的最后一句话，是对已不在人世的拉伊哈的爱的宣言。全书以对过去的怀念结束：在失去的伊斯坦布尔，与拉伊哈共度的失去的幸福时光。麦夫鲁特与妻子共享的伊斯坦布尔几乎消失了；但他仍在尚存一息的老街道上追寻它的遗迹。这已不是拉伊哈曾生活的伊斯坦布尔；或者说，在这个改变了的伊斯坦布尔，拉伊哈已不再生活。很难分辨哪一个在先。
en: The imagery in Mevlut’s dreams is another detail reinforcing the nostalgia in the ending of the novel. As mentioned above, in his dreams Mevlut sees Rayiha in an old mansion, which is one of the ultimate symbols of the picturesque old Istanbul. He cannot reach her in the dream, as the streets he walks keep changing. In these motifs of constant change, and the impossibility of finding the beloved, it is possible to find a reference to his love for an Istanbul which has mostly faded away. The setting of the very last scene of the book is a street around Feriköy which extends to the Golden Horn. These streets are at an intersecting point where Muslim and former minority neighbourhoods meet. They are places which have not been completely destroyed by urban transformation yet, and still have a touch of the old Istanbul. Mevlut’s final words, which are also the final words of the novel, are his declaration of love for Rayiha, who is no longer in this world. The book ends with a longing for the past: lost happy times with Rayiha, in a lost Istanbul. The Istanbul Mevlut shared with his wife has almost disappeared; however, he is tracking its remnants in the old streets which are still, albeit barely, alive. This is not the Istanbul where Rayiha once lived; or, Rayiha no longer lives in this changed Istanbul. It is difficult to dissect which comes first.

zh: 帕慕克以描写麦夫鲁特对伊斯坦布尔深厚的爱，结束《我脑袋里的怪东西》，由此强调城市权利概念。城市属于那些能够欣赏它的美与遗产的人；城市权利并不只包含物质需要，也包含把城市作为
